story.title: The forest, in our hands
story.subtitle: Where amber, incense, and quiet attention meet.
story.p1: Each piece begins with a conversation in the forest. From Baltic amber to Yunnan agarwood, from Malaysian rattan to the spice routes of the Middle East — we travel far to bring nature's breath to you.
story.p2: The forest is not the backdrop. It is the protagonist. Wear one amber, light one incense — the forest lives.
story.p3: We do not chase luxury. We chase translucence, breath, and the stillness of the East. Handcraft, slowness, and respect for nature are the truest form of luxury.
story.p4: To wear one of our pieces is to remember: the forest is patient. We should be too.
story.pull_quote: Wear one amber, light one incense — the forest lives.

vision.title: A forest that travels with you
vision.subtitle: What we are quietly working toward.
vision.p1: We imagine a world where every piece of adornment is so different, you cannot find two alike. Each one carries a memory of the place it came from — the resin of a tree that lived a million years ago, the smoke of a forest that still stands.
vision.p2: We are not building a fashion brand. We are cultivating a relationship between the East and the wild — between the patience of a tree and the patience of a wearer.
vision.p3: Five years from now, we hope a hundred thousand people will wear our work. That they will slow down when they fasten an amber clasp. That they will pause when they light an incense stick.
vision.p4: When you wear one amber, light one incense — the forest lives.

amber.title: Amber — a frozen breath of forests
amber.subtitle: A frozen breath of ancient forests, worn on your skin.
amber.p1: Amber is a vessel of time. It preserves resin, bubbles, insect wings, and forest light from forty million years ago. Baltic coast amber contains 3–8% succinic acid, which medieval Europeans called the 'shield against illness' — 'gold of the North'.
amber.p2: Burmese Hukawng Valley amber dates from the mid-Cretaceous — even older. Dominican blue amber glows with a quiet fluorescence under UV light, rare and prized. Chinese Fushun amber and Sicilian amber each carry the temperament of their soil.
amber.p3: We choose ours by one standard: how translucent the light passes through. Every piece comes with its origin and age — so the wearer is not just wearing jewelry, but a piece of nature's memory.

incense.title: Eastern incense — smoke that remembers the mountains
incense.subtitle: Smoke that remembers the mountains.
incense.p1: Incense traces back to ancient ritual in China and India. Han dynasty boshan censers, Tang dynasty incense ceremonies, Song scholars burning incense while reading — a thread of smoke has traveled through a thousand years and is still part of our daily life.
incense.p2: Agarwood is the resin secreted by wounded trees, transformed by time. It is called 'the diamond of plants.' Yunnan, Hainan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Laos — each region produces a different fragrance: cool, mellow, sweet, or bitter. We select by two standards: translucence, and depth of layer.
incense.p3: Sticks, balms, essential oils, burners — the forms differ; the essence is the same: let the air remember the stillness of the forest.

craft.title: The patience of the hand
craft.p1: Our craft begins with stone selection. Each piece of amber and each piece of wood is examined under direct light to exclude cracks, impurities, and signs of artificial enhancement.
craft.p2: Cutting prioritizes preserving maximum translucence. We do not chase the most cuts from one stone — every cut must respect the weight of time. Grinding proceeds through coarse, fine, and polishing stages, repeatedly checking grain under a loupe to avoid removing what should remain.
craft.p3: Holes are drilled at manual speeds to avoid thermal fracturing. Knots between beads use traditional Chinese knotting — even tension, rarely loose.
craft.p4: Incense blending follows classical recipes: agarwood and sandalwood as base, with clove, borneol, and licorice as modifiers. The wrong ratio, and the fragrance loses its depth.
craft.p5: We believe: slowness is respect for nature.

materials.title: Where the materials come from
materials.intro: Six origins, each with its own temperament.
materials.amber_baltic_desc: 3–8% succinic acid, warm tones, common honey and pale amber. Sources: Lithuania, Latvia, Poland, Denmark.
materials.amber_burma_desc: Mid-Cretaceous, very old. Deep red, dark brown, wine tones; rich in inclusions.
materials.amber_dominican_desc: Quiet blue fluorescence under UV. Rare; the most valuable.
materials.amber_fushun_desc: From Liaoning Fushun's open-pit coal mine, deep tones, near-depleted, collected value.
materials.amber_sicily_desc: Rich in plant debris, dark red tones, Mediterranean Italian character.
materials.agarwood_desc: Yunnan, Hainan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Laos — each region's fragrance differs. Selected by translucence and depth.
